Subject: MAP: draft & initial capacity ask

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, I put together a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (attached) that ties the evaluation milestones to the capacity reservation milestones so we can line up procurement lead times with your acceptance windows. High level:

- Evaluation window: 8/2 – 9/15 (pilot traffic, latency and quality targets)
- Required pool at kick: 8 x H100 (burst to 12) to cover inference + eval re-runs
- Target steady-state: 24 x H100 by 11/01; fallback profile on A100 if H100 leadtime slips
- Acceptance criteria: latency P95 < 150ms for 8k context on 8x H100, throughput >= 1200 toks/s aggregate, quality delta vs benchmark < 2%

Please review the attached MAP spreadsheet (tabbed by milestone). Key asks for Helios ops: confirm preferred region (us-west/us-east), any org-level restrictions on reserved capacity, and whether you want a single tranche or two tranches (Aug + Oct).

I'll loop in Irene to confirm the acceptance tests and Marissa for the procurement cadence if we need a deviation on standard SLAs.

Next step: if you can comment on the spreadsheet by Tue 8/3 EOD, we'll lock in the draft and scope the DocuSign for the reservation commitment.

Attachments: Helios_MAP_draft_v1.xlsx (MAP, timelines, tentative pricing)

Best,
Jordan

Thanks for the clear draft. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) Region: prefer us-east for lower egress latency to our product region, but we can take a hybrid approach if you recommend it for availability.
2) Tranches: ops prefers a two-tranche approach — 8 units on day one (pilot), then top-up to 24 in October; downside: longer runway to ramp means we need a guaranteed hold window for tranche 2 pricing.
3) Workload: most of our test calls will be multi-turn chat + long-context embeddings; initial perf gating should include cold-start tails for KV cache at 8k tokens.

We reviewed your acceptance criteria and they look reasonable; ops will run a short checklist against the MAP and push comments inline in the spreadsheet by EOD Thu 8/5.

Hi Sarah / Jordan —

I reviewed the MAP and ops notes. A few technical points and rungs we should include in the acceptance criteria to make the evaluation deterministic:

- Bench harness: we will provide a JMeter/locust harness and a reproducible prompt set (50k tokens total across eval cases).
- Cold-start test: 30 cold-restarts across the 8-node pool to measure KV warmup tail distribution; acceptance if P99 cold-start < 1.2x warm cache P99.
- Throughput validation: run 3 sustained 30-minute windows at target concurrency. If throughput falls <90% of target in 2/3 windows, we mark an engineering gate and run a remediation loop (latency profiling, kernel changes).
- Fallback profile: we will prepare an A100 profile with 25% lower batch size and quantized weights; that will be the automatic fallback if H100 availability slips beyond agreed lead time.
- Lead times: current vendor quotes for H100 delivery to dedicated pools are ~10–14 weeks from order. A100 (or pre-quantized H100 equivalent) is ~4–6 weeks. We should plan tranche 2 ordering no later than Aug 30 to meet Nov 1 steady-state.

Attachments: SOC2_summary_for_helios.pdf (security/compliance snapshot to help your procurement).

I'll also propose a short acceptance playbook:
- 8/16: Pilot cutover, sanity checks (1 day)
- 8/17–9/01: Perf & quality window (2 weeks)
- 9/02–9/08: Fixes and re-run gating tests
- 9/09: Acceptance decision and tranche-2 order go/no-go

If Helios wants a non-standard SLA window during the pilot (e.g., lower latency SLO), we should capture that as an SLA exception in the MAP so procurement can include it in contract language.

Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
